method: Independent scripts in scratch/fund_runs/0001803498/reviewer_bcpc/: outstanding.py (ledger + digest), ctx_hits.sql (rows each context-keyed correction reaches, by context and by identifier), diffcols.sql (rg1b vs bcpc by row_id, by accounting_record_class), shares_check.py (every row whose shares_held or source changed, against the printed line), name_triple.py (each published row located by its printed cost/fair-value pair; issuer token must precede it), quotes_all.py (every quote in the report incl. resolved investigations). Not done: the 20-row random page sample (orchestrator item); no cohort-wide measurement of the two shared-code changes.

finding_reviews.rationale: Flagged population reconstructed from shadow/page_rule_findings.csv. bcpa (before fixes) flagged 10 rows at 2022-09-30: ROW-6900c35a75241a00, 9b3f907105946796, fc5ed563201e24c2, fb32f9352d6dcfba, 5f21d87df1a292ee, 61d62c10a7bc6e3f, e35d920e2cf24a7e, a9eb1394671b13f4, fa9769dd8e6bbcd0, 4b75e14edadd61fc; all 10 are in affected_rows. bcpc flags 2: ROW-6900c35a75241a00 (Minerva) and ROW-fb32f9352d6dcfba (Petco), both covered. The 8 context-only keys are unflagged misnamed rows found by value triple; they match 8 of the 16 context-keyed issuer_name corrections at 2022-09-30. Independent check name_triple.py over all 722 published 2022-09-30 rows: 720 have their issuer printed before their cost/FV pair, 1 mismatch (Minerva), Petco passes on token 'petco'. Over all 15,499 published BCRED rows in all quarters: 1 mismatch (the same Minerva row), 4 pairs not on page, so no further misnamed rows found by this method. Context-keyed corrections: each of the 31 (accession, context) keys hits exactly one row, all parent_schedule; the 6 identifiers shared with JV-schedule rows (PSKW, Radnet, Reverb, Smile Doctors, Stepping Stones, Surgery Centers) leave the underlying_schedule twins untouched (no corrected_fields, original names). rg1b vs bcpc diff: 0 changes of any compared field on 9,173 underlying_schedule rows. Proposals checked on the page: PD-...-1 Petco: current line prints the truncated 'Petco Health and Wellness Comp' with 4,870/4,860/4,612 = published row; member 'Petco Health & Wellness Co, Inc.'; prior quarter (0001803498-22-000017) prints the full name on the same amortising loan (4,882 par), so same issuer is right. PD-...-2 Minerva: member 'Minerva Merger Sub, Inc.', page prints 'Athenahealth, Inc.' under Unsecured Debt with 7,146/7,146/5,663, 2/15/2030 = published row; bcpb (rename applied) puts this row at the head of position d9953922 (the 2029 term loan, 2022-12-31 to 2026-06-30) and moves the 2022-09-30 term loan (38,951 par) to a separate position 9901d72c; bcpc restores the rg1b chains. Both proposals are factually right. Conclusion source_ambiguity is reasonable (member vs page name both defensible). Caveats, not grounds for rejection: (1) the report's counts are off by one: it says 19 misnamed / 17 fixed, but bcpc renames 16 rows at 2022-09-30 and leaves 2 (18, matching affected_rows); (2) the Minerva proposal rests on a matcher defect, recorded as observation position-chain-follows-shifted-member, not on the name being right; (3) corrected rows still chain to the member's company (Stepping Stones 2022-09-30 to The Fertility Partners 2022-12-31 in d7e4c545; Surgery Centers to Fertility in 3a1f21b8), so position_id on those rows stays wrong.

Detector units_printed (candidate_rules.unit_count_differs_from_row_text, kind proxy_count_not_on_row) exists and flagged all 16 quarters in bcpa, so existing_detector is right. observation_reviews.rationale: Confirmed the shifted runs on the page and in bcpc (16 renamed rows at 2022-09-30, listed by context in ctx_hits.sql). My own implementation of the proposed value-triple check (name_triple.py, first distinctive name token within 170 characters before the printed cost/FV pair) over all 15,499 published BCRED rows returned 1 mismatch (Minerva, a real member/page difference) and 4 unlocated pairs, so the false-alarm rate on this fund is low and the check is independent of the member join. propose_detector with a concrete suggested_check is the right decision. Note it is a proxy: a loose token test can pass a shifted row whose neighbour shares a first word.

observation_reviews.rationale: The facts are right: 6 identifiers repeat on an underlying_schedule row of 0001803498-22-000021 (ctx_hits.sql shows n_ident_rows = 2 for PSKW, Radnet, Reverb, Smile Doctors, Stepping Stones, Surgery Centers), and the context-keyed file kept the JV twins untouched. The detection decision is not supported: 'existing_detector' points at the _apply_row_corrections warning 'Row correction matches %d rows (expected 1) ... applying to all matches', which logs and then applies the correction to every match. Nothing stops it: fund_gate.check_corrections reads only 'Row correction unmatched' lines. The report's own rationale says 'the guard is a warning, not a stop'. A recurrence would rename JV rows, caught at best by the declared-changes diff. The decision should be propose_detector, using the suggested_check already given (refuse a multi-match identifier spec, or make check_corrections fail on 'expected 1' lines for the fund).

The Minerva rename effect is confirmed in bcpb (notes put at the head of d9953922, 2022-09-30 term loan split to 9901d72c). No rule checks issuer and maturity continuity in a chain, so propose_detector with the stated check is right. action 'left' means these position_ids stay wrong in the published data; that should stay visible to the owner.

observation_reviews.rationale: The observation itself is plausible (Gulf Stream Meridian tranches are printed under Structured Finance Obligations) and was not re-measured here. The detection decision is wrong: 'existing_detector' cites 'observations.py structured-credit-classed-as-direct-lending', but scripts/v05_evidence/observations.py is the observations log, not a check, and the rationale itself says 'no ledger rule yet'. Nothing would catch a recurrence. The decision should be propose_detector using the suggested_check already given (rows printed under a structured-finance heading must not be DIRECT_LENDING), measured for false alarms before it is relied on.

The fact is right: the 6 rows that got maturity_date by correction (PSKW->PPV, Radnet->PSKW, Reverb->Radnet, Smile->Reverb, Stepping Stones->SpecialtyCare, Surgery Centers->SpecialtyCare contexts) publish a day-precision date. The decision 'not_feasible' is not supported. A check is trivially feasible and has no false-alarm risk: maturity_status 'unresolved' with a valid day-precision maturity_date. The rationale's 'no consumer reads it' is also contradicted by the code: pipeline/financial_validation.py tests maturity_status against maturity_date (e.g. 'not_disclosed' with a date fails), and pipeline/categorical_field_assessment.py assesses it. Either propose the check, or point existing_detector at financial_validation and extend it to the 'unresolved'-with-date case.

Page: the 10/20/2034 tranche (4,250 / 4,069 / 3,587) is printed 'OCP CLO 2020-22, Ltd.' and the next tranche 'OCP CLO 2021-22, Ltd.'. The contexts list members 'OCP CLO 2021-22, Ltd. 1' and '... 2' only, and the 2021-12-31 comparative prints 2021-22, so a page typo is the likely reading and leaving the member name is right. Detecting a digit difference is possible, but every hit would need an outside reference to resolve, and the row is 3.6M. not_feasible is acceptable.
